title: Bobkov inequality for Boolean arrays
statement: Let $I$ and $J$ be finite sets and let $f:\{0,1\}^{I\times J}\to\mathbb R$ take values in $[0,1]$. Under independent uniform bits, let $\mathbb E f$ denote its expectation and define $D_{ij}f(x)=\bigl(f(x^{ij\leftarrow0})-f(x^{ij\leftarrow1})\bigr)/2$, where $x^{ij\leftarrow b}$ is obtained by setting coordinate $(i,j)$ to $b$. Then $\overline I(\mathbb E f)\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}(D_{ij}f)^2}$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite index sets I and J
A real-valued function on Boolean arrays indexed by I × J
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and let $\overline I(p)=\varphi(\Phi^{-1}(p))$ for $0<p<1$, with $\overline I(p)=0$ elsewhere. Let $I,J$ be finite and $f:\{0,1\}^{I\times J}\to[0,1]$. Under independent uniform bits, $\overline I(\mathbb E f)\le\mathbb E\sqrt{\overline I(f)^2+\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}(D_{ij}f)^2}$, where $D_{ij}f(x)=(f(x^{ij\leftarrow0})-f(x^{ij\leftarrow1}))/2$.
